"Discourse on Comprehending the Yì"
Master Ruǎn said:
What is the Yì?
It is the mysterious truth of antiquity,
the classic of changes from the distant past.
When Fúxī Shì witnessed an end of heaven and earth,
and beheld the exhaustion of all beings,
with resources no longer preserved,
and laws obscured and dim,
the virtue of the spiritual and bright not penetrating,
the sentiments of all ages not in harmony;
thus he first created the eight trigrams.
Extending and expanding them,
touching upon categories and lengthening them,
dividing the yīn and yáng,
ordering the firm and yielding,
accumulating mountains and marshes,
connecting water and fire,
mixing and unifying them,
transforming and penetrating them,
ending with Wèijì (Incomplete),
the sixty-four hexagrams exhaust yet never end.
Hence, heaven and earth take form and all things take shape,
fortune and misfortune appear, and regret and remorse arise,
affairs find their application,
and transformations achieve completion.
Facing south to hear and judge,
governing toward the light;
tying knots to make nets and traps,
attaining the goods of the midday market,
cultivating the benefits of the plow and share to teach,
so all under heaven could find their proper place.
Huángdì, Yáo, and Shùn responded to their times and attended to their duties,
each had their appropriations,
exhausting the spiritual and knowing the transformative,
they narrated according to the celestial order.
Fúxī Shì laid out and elaborated the changes of the sixty-four hexagrams;
later sages observed and followed them,
taking them as images and applying them.
The classics of Yǔ and Tāng are still extant,
yet the texts of high antiquity do not survive;
until King Wén,
who thus appended the explanations,
whereupon the era of the Guīcáng passed and the Zhōu classics arose.
Above and below are not constant,
the firm and yielding exchange places,
one cannot take them as fixed norms,
only change finds its fit,
therefore it is called "Yì" (Change).
The Book of Changes as a text
roots itself in heaven and earth,
follows the principles of yīn and yáng,
deduces the cycles of prosperity and decline,
emerging from obscurity to reach clarity and prominence.
Thus, in the initial phase of Qián, "the hidden dragon should not act,"
signifying that the virtue of the great person remains concealed and not yet revealed,
latent and not yet expressed,
awaiting the right time to rise,
moving in accordance with change.
Once heaven and earth were established,
Zhūn and Méng hexagrams began to appear,
Xū teaches waiting for the opportune moment,
Sòng establishes righteousness,
Shī gathers the masses,
Bǐ brings peace to the people,
hence "the ancient kings established myriad states,
befriended the feudal lords,"
to win their hearts.
By tracing origins and accumulating,
nurturing and regulating,
harmony is achieved between high and low,
"shaping the ways of heaven and earth,
assisting the appropriateness of heaven and earth to guide the people,"
following their inherent principles.
After the ancient kings passed away,
virtue and laws became distorted and altered,
superiors oppressed inferiors, and subordinates were neglected,
rulers and ministers lost control,
the firm and yielding lost harmony,
heaven and earth ceased to interact,
thus the noble person sought unity in diversity,
suppressing evil and promoting good,
to achieve greatness.
Through humility, one shines,
reducing the excessive to benefit the deficient,
honoring the sage and virtuous to command,
as thunder emerges from the earth,
then the great person attains position,
enlightened sages rise again,
so the ancient kings created music to offer to the Supreme Deity,
illuminating their way to repay heaven's favor.
Thereupon, all things submit,
following and serving,
sons obeying their fathers,
ministers upholding their rulers,
governing with unity,
observing the world comprehensively,
thus the ancient kings inspected regions, observed the people, and established teachings,
regulating with measures.
Embracing and containing all,
uniting and encompassing,
the ancient kings used this to clarify punishments and enforce laws.
From above to below,
the noble return to the humble,
beauty completes, prosperity ends,
the extreme time arrives with the solstice,
the ancient kings closed the passes,
merchants did not travel,
the ruler did not inspect the regions,
to calm the people.
In the declining end of an era,
plans do not succeed,
responding to fate and following heaven,
acting without recklessness,
thus the ancient kings diligently responded to the seasons to nurture all things,
spreading benevolence and grace to establish their virtue.
All things return and follow,
like laws flowing and continuing,
nurturing good and reversing evil,
benefits accumulate and breed harm,
excessive firmness loses its grip,
Kǎn hexagram positions through repetition,
those above lose their way,
those below lose their community,
then the great person continues the light,
shining upon the four directions,
displaying their virtue.
Since the beginning of Qián,
its application is balanced and clear,
prosperity and decline have their times,
firmness and yielding are not constant,
sometimes gain, sometimes loss,
one yīn, one yáng,
emerging and entering, auspicious and inauspicious,
from darkness to discernible clarity;
when culture and brightness reach their limit,
having wings but not flying,
following it ensures survival,
those who take it will return,
applying it with gentleness,
using it in subtlety,
valuing change and caution in small matters,
interacting with things in mutual pursuit;
only those who know the future and store the past can fully comprehend it.
The Book of Changes as a text
encompasses the ways of heaven and earth,
embracing the nature of all things.
When the Way reaches its limit, it reverses;
when affairs reach their extreme, they change.
"Reversal" responds to the times,
"change" addresses pressing needs.
By responding to the times,
all under heaven look up to its blessings;
by addressing pressing needs,
all things rely on its benefits.
When blessings are bestowed, all under heaven submit,
this is how heaven follows spontaneity,
benefiting living beings.
Wealth and honor matching heaven and earth,
achievements and fame filling the universe,
none can topple them,
none can harm them,
for they do not oppose the Way.
Heaven and earth
are the masters of the Changes,
all things
are the heart of the Changes;
thus emptiness receives them,
resonance harmonizes them.
Male below, female above,
communicates their energies;
softness supporting firmness,
prolongs their kinds;
compliantly maintaining them,
withdrawing when retreating.
Above abundant, below accumulated,
firm movement brings great strength.
Upright and great must be employed,
when strength peaks, expectations rise;
bright ascension means advancement,
when overly brilliant, injury follows;
gathering to settle oneself,
differentiation to form categories.
When separation is resolved,
slackness becomes failure.
Increase and decrease have their seasons,
discernment governs their application.
Proclaiming in the royal court,
riding five horses to defeat.
When firmness overcomes softness,
above seeks, below joins,
ministers encounter enlightened rulers,
softness meets firmness,
all things flourish.
Firmness occupying central correctness,
greatly practiced under heaven,
hence later used to issue decrees to the four states,
valuing the teaching of separation.
Thereupon heaven and earth gather,
the common people unite in function,
ascending without cease,
reaching the extreme and descending,
the well nourishes endlessly,
lowliness cannot penetrate,
so change is necessary.
Reform creates vessels,
noble and humble have their distinctions,
elder and younger their order.
Led by Zhèn,
guarded by authority.
Action cannot persist endlessly,
responding to opposition while proceeding.
Gradually advancing,
seeking position for people,
this is the gentleman's desire for advancement.
The minister seeking the ruler,
yin following yang,
entrusting with sincere submission,
then finds proper place.
Return and respond,
focus and unify,
yang virtue receives submission,
the Way abundant, position great.
Worthy persons and gentlemen,
with followers achieve greatness.
Extravagance exhausts the grandee's position,
grouped yet without acceptance,
accepted yet without place.
Humbling oneself, lowering intentions,
benefits from meeting the great person.
Xùn to proclaim commands,
softly complying with firmness.
Entering and delighting,
delighting and teaching,
complying and responding to people.
Dispersing to form patterns,
wind moving over water,
having pattern and radiance,
male action endless,
female position external,
multiple yin supporting the fifth,
above united in the center,
from the beginning renewing,
riding wood with merit,
thus ancient kings sacrificed to the Lord,
established temples,
serving heaven to build the state.
Firm and soft appropriately centered,
regulated by measures,
the Way remains endless.
Trust and affection binding inwardly,
firm gaining central position,
sincerity arising from the heart,
all things follow their kinds.
Great gain brings loss,
excessive advance brings error,
already responding to the distant,
silence brings no benefit,
thus the gentleman emphasizes reverence in conduct,
emphasizes grief in mourning,
sincerity overcomes falsity.
Xiǎoguò below Tài,
unsuitable above,
below stopping, above moving,
resembling flying birds.
Initial six, Kǎn below,
top six, Lí body,
flying birds bringing misfortune,
thus calamity arises.
Soft occupying center,
firm losing position,
beneficial to move with the times,
transgressing yet wanting success,
small prosperity, correct image,
yin all riding yang,
yang firmness being replaced,
ruler and minister exchanging positions,
chaos without end,
this is not what centrality means,
thus the gentleman anticipates troubles and prevents them,
considering potential failures.
Penetrating change endlessly,
completing decay and beginning anew,
firm not yet emerged,
yin in the center,
soft assistance not neglected,
thus crossing without end,
modeling Hé Tú and Luò Shū,
divine objects establishing teachings that all under heaven follow.
Carefully discerning positions,
yin and yang seeking each other,
initially following the Way,
the origin of distant achievements.
The hexagram forms open and close,
with Qián taking one as opening,
and Kūn taking two as closing.
When Qián and Kūn form their bodies, strength and softness have their positions.
Thus wood ages at Wèi,
water is born at Shēn,
and Kūn resides in the southwest;
fire ages at Xū,
wood is born at Hài,
and Qián resides in the northwest;
this is the boundary of strength and softness,
hence they are called father and mother.
Yang receives Zhèn's movement,
emerging and succeeding one another,
sovereign control is then exercised,
and all things flourish,
hence it is called the eldest son;
water ages at Chén,
metal is born at Sì,
a single breath preserves it,
ending and then rising again,
so Xùn is the eldest daughter;
Zhèn emerges from wind,
yin virtue has its order,
the quail calls within fire,
the mother's way is about to begin,
so Lí is the middle daughter;
again in the northwest,
vigorous battle is about to ascend,
the youngest yin is tender and obscure,
declining and unable to prevail,
so Duì is the youngest daughter.
Drawing from the granary's store,
initiating darkness into yang,
centered but not yet reached,
contained but not yet manifest,
so Kǎn is the middle son;
circulating and connecting,
all things having ended,
creating subtlety for a new beginning,
bright but not yet glowing,
so Gèn is the youngest son.
Qián is round, Kūn is square,
women soft, men firm,
strength and softness shift with time,
and fortune or calamity follow;
following transformation, one knows life,
observing change, one sees demise;
thus auspiciousness, misfortune, success, and failure
cannot be disordered.
What is Dàguò?
The ridgepole bends with no support,
the great is excessive.
The ancient kings in governing the world
established penalties but had no offenders,
set punishments but did not apply them,
in Xí Kǎn, firmness is central,
only through the heart is there smoothness,
the king rectifies his virtue,
the lords guard their duties,
superiors and inferiors have no doubts,
ministers and ruler are without confusion.
Presenting offerings through the window,
not through the door—what blame is there?
Chariots and riders at the central gate,
swords and halberds in the court,
even if surrounded by thorns,
misfortune has lasted three years,
the top six loses the way,
punishment is decided.
Thus Gāozōng campaigned against Guǐfāng,
the soft way is central;
after three years, there was reward,
virtue was then abundant.
Tóngrén's fifth call,
thinks of its end;
Lǚ's top beauty,
rejoices in its extremity.
Therefore, those who err in punishment are strict but not restrained,
those who lose virtue are high but not respected,
so the gentleman upholds righteousness to maintain his position,
consolidates laws to awe the people,
which path then brings smoothness?
Destroying ears leads to misfortune.
What is Xiǎoguò?
Overstepping position and encroaching upon superiors,
harming the upright and endangering oneself,
the small is excessive.
Why does Jìjì's first six end in disorder?
Water over the sun,
three yin riding on yang,
striving to cross by force,
not stopping ensures ruin,
hence initial auspiciousness ends in disorder.
Wèijì's top six,
drinking wine incurs no blame,
why?
Having erred but not corrected,
in danger yet not alert,
who is to blame for it!
What is Wúwàng?
Arriving without expectation,
not by the meeting of yin and yang's contrary course.
The third six,
the disaster of no falsehood,
a tethered ox,
a passerby takes it,
the villager suffers disaster,
why?
Having a state but not gathering its people,
having a multitude but not maintaining its tools,
a passerby takes it—
is that not a disaster?
The fifth nine's illness needs no medicine,
why?
An extraordinary richness,
separating to unite,
the illness of no falsehood,
disaster to eliminate misfortune,
heaven's timing decides success or failure,
what can medicine achieve?
No medicine brings joy,
without accomplishment, what is there to recognize?
What is the dragon?
It is the category of yang's vigor,
a metaphor for sublime virtue and noble dignity.
Matched with heaven's abundance,
sublime virtue unsurpassed is called noble dignity.
The great person receives the mandate,
residing centrally and facing the yang,
this is the ultimate of virtue.
Why does the overreaching dragon have regret?
Inheriting and maintaining received nobility,
one possesses the cause but virtue is not fulfilled.
Desiring greatness without regard for the small,
indulging in luxury without considering scarcity,
occupying the correct high position without humility,
having noble toil without foundation,
losing will and endangering oneself,
thus there is regret.
What are the former kings?
They are the achievements of great persons.
Hence establishing myriad states,
befriending the feudal lords,
they erected their righteousness;
creating music and offering to the Supreme Deity,
they rectified their mandate;
inspecting regions and observing the people,
they implemented their decrees;
clarifying punishments and regulating laws,
they supervised their governance;
closing passes and not traveling,
they calmed the disorderly people;
flourishing in season and nurturing virtue,
they responded to manifest their blessings;
serving the Deity and establishing temples,
they displayed their emoluments.
What is called the creations of the sage kings
does not refer to inheriting peace.
What is the sovereign?
The accomplished ruler securing the position,
relying on the enterprise and cultivating institutions,
preserving teachings and upholding laws,
accumulating practices to bring about order and stability.
Thus naturally achieving success and fulfilling utility,
having reached great penetration,
the sovereign completes the ways of heaven and earth to assist the people.
Accomplishing transformation and managing decisions,
issuing decrees and proclamations to the regions,
continuing the lineage and succeeding in decline.
Centrally handling affairs to be rectified,
not responding to the initial reception of the mandate.
What is the superior?
Sun and moon alternate,
prosperity and decline follow each other,
excessive ornamentation means benefits not yet received swiftly,
thus the king and sovereign are not named,
the noble person does not err,
the superior enriches the inferior,
the way is natural.
What is the noble person?
Assisting the sage and supporting the mandate,
aiding teachings and clarifying laws,
observing the times to act,
possessing the way and serving as a minister.
Following correct virtue to manage righteousness,
examining danger and decline to guard oneself,
thus managing affairs to rectify fullness,
acting resolutely to fulfill righteousness,
eating and drinking while awaiting the proper time,
distinguishing righteousness to undertake tasks,
all are means to display the former kings' establishment of states,
and assist the sage's divine will.
Perceiving danger and considering difficulties,
contemplating perils and taking precautions,
distinguishing things and residing in the proper place,
being cautious at the start and reverent in beginnings,
all are conducts of ministers,
not the way of the great ruler.
What is the great person?
The dragon virtue covertly penetrates,
noble and base communicate clearly,
having position without title,
acting greatly,
thus great excess extinguishes and reveals the world's hidden and manifest,
the great person emits double radiance,
continuing brightness to illuminate the four directions,
all things look up and live,
combining virtue with heaven and earth,
accomplishing without acting,
thus the great person transforms like a tiger,
heavenly virtue rises.
The noble person says:
"The Yì,
conforms to heaven and earth,
orders the myriad things,
square and round have proper forms,
the four seasons have constant positions,
undertakings have their attachments,
birds and beasts have their gatherings,
thus all things are without exception unified.
Yīn and yáng generate nature,
nature thus has hardness and softness;
hardness and softness generate feelings,
feelings thus have love and aversion.
Love and aversion generate gain and loss,
gain and loss generate regret and distress,
regret and distress become evident and fortune or misfortune appear.
The eight trigrams reside in positions to rectify nature,
the yarrow stalks and tortoise shell are comprehensively penetrating to seek feelings.
Feelings and nature interact and advantage and harm emerge,
thus establishing benevolence and righteousness to fix nature,
adopting yarrow and tortoise to control feelings.
Benevolence and righteousness have pairs and calamity and fortune divide,
therefore the sage uses them to establish the positions under heaven,
fix the system of noble and base,
order the appropriateness of yīn and yáng,
distinguish the nodes of hardness and softness.
Those who follow it survive,
those who oppose it perish,
those who attain it have safety of person,
those who lose it face personal danger.
Thus those who violate it to seek separately,
though seemingly fortunate will inevitably meet misfortune;
those who know it and maintain steadfastness,
though in straits will inevitably penetrate.
Thus solitude is the master of virtue,
wantonness is the source of harm,
advancing is the beginning of return,
exhaustion is the root of beginning.
Therefore what has not arrived cannot be split,
what is already used cannot be surpassed.
Zhòu possessed the title of the world,
yet was comparable to the category of commoners,
neighboring Zhōu occupied the humble status of a small marquis,
yet enjoyed the guest position at the Western Mountains.
The responses of internal and external had already been applied,
yet the names of noble and base were not divided,
why?
The way of heaven had not reached its end,
good and evil were not yet pure.
Therefore those who understand the way of heaven have no desires,
those who examine the virtue of humans have no worries.
Being above without oppressing those below,
staying humble without offending the noble,
thus the way cannot be opposed,
virtue cannot be violated.
Therefore the sage stands alone without distress,
in great crowds does not increase,
releasing it yet the way remains,
using it yet it cannot be exhausted.
Viewing from this,
the Yì is thereby penetrated.
"Tōng Lǎo Lùn"
The sage understands the principles of heaven and humanity,
comprehends the distinctions of the natural,
penetrates the substance of governance and transformation,
examines the teachings of great caution,
thus ruler and minister reign with folded hands,
preserving the simplicity of the pristine essence,
the common people are cheerful and preserve the harmony of their nature and life.
○"Imperial Readings" 1.
The Dào,
models the natural in effecting transformation,
if lords and kings can uphold it,
the myriad things will transform spontaneously.
The "Yì" calls it "Tàijí",
the "Chūnqiū" calls it "Yuán",
Lǎozǐ calls it "Dào".
○"Imperial Readings" 1.
The Three Sovereigns relied on the Dào,
the Five Emperors wielded virtue,
the Three Kings implemented benevolence,
the Five Hegemons practiced righteousness,
the powerful states employed wisdom:
such are the differences in superiority and inferiority,
the decline in richness and thickness.
○"Imperial Readings" 77.
"Dá Zhuāng Lùn"
In the time of Yīdān'è,
the year of Zhíxú,
when the myriad things were beginning,
in the distant night month of late autumn,
the master wandered and soared,
riding the wind to roam,
went following above the Chìshuǐ River,
came ascending the Yǐnbèn Hill,
approached the winding ridge path,
gazed upon the vast marshland,
halted as if in a trance,
stopped suddenly,
not recognizing why he traveled before,
why he stayed now;
disconsolate and without joy,
sorrowful, he returned to plain simplicity.
In daytime leisure at home,
leaning on a table, he played the qin.
Thereupon, the curious gentlemen of officialdom heard of this,
and together they discussed composing phrases and combining sentences,
to raise their usual doubts.
Then they straightened their attire and adjusted their appearance,
gnashing their teeth as they stepped forward,
pushing through by age, treading on each other's heels,
following one another as they advanced together.
They walked with an air of grandeur,
gazed with keen scrutiny,
planted their feet and stepped onto the stairs,
hurrying as if soaring to arrive.
They sat shoulder to shoulder,
sleeves respectfully arranged and postures restrained,
hesitating and eyeing each other like trees in a forest,
none willing to speak first.
One man,
the most outstanding among them,
fiercely glared and struck a pose, proclaiming loudly:
"I was born after the era of Táng Yú,
grew up among the descendants of Wén Wǔ,
traveled during the prosperity of Chéng Kāng,
and thrive in the present age.
I recite the teachings of the Six Classics,
practice the ways of our Confucian tradition,
dressed in scholarly robes,
crowned with flying-feather hats,
draped in curved hems,
and have long displayed dual egret insignias;
yet I have not heard the essence of the ultimate Dao,
that differs from this!
Moreover, the great praise it,
the common people follow it.
I wish to hear the supreme teaching,
to resolve my doubts."
The master said:
"What is it
that you doubt?"
The guest replied:
"The Way of Heaven values life,
the Way of Earth values constancy,
the sages cultivate these,
to establish their reputation.
Fortune and misfortune have their distinctions,
right and wrong have their principles,
striving for benefit and high status,
detesting death and cherishing life,
thus the world is at peace and great achievements are made.
Now Zhuāng Zhōu equates misfortune and fortune and unifies life and death,
treating heaven and earth as one entity,
and all things as a single concept,
is this not delusional and losing the truth,
while considering oneself sincere?"
Thereupon the master stroked his zither with ease,
sighed with emotion,
lowered his head with a slight smile,
raised it and let his gaze wander,
inhaled and exhaled to gather his spirit,
and spoke of what he perceived:
"In the past, there was one who wished to gaze from the peak of Làng,
equipped with formal caps,
and riding Huá Liú horses,
reaching beneath Kūnlún,
only to vanish and not return.
Formal caps
are ordinary ceremonial attire;
Huá Liú horses
are merely common steeds;
they are not means to soar over the heights of Zēngchéng,
or wander within Xuán Pǔ.
Moreover, the light of the Zhū Lóng
does not illuminate a single hall,
and the mouth of the Cháng Mountain
does not speak in winding chambers.
Now I shall dismantle the towering heights,
block the flowing expanses,
speak of your origins,
hoping you may awaken and grasp it!
Heaven and earth are born from nature,
and all things are born from heaven and earth.
Nature has no exterior,
hence heaven and earth are named;
heaven and earth have an interior,
thus all things are born.
When there is no exterior,
who can speak of difference?
When there is an interior,
who can speak of distinction?
The earth flows with dryness,
the heaven resists with moisture.
The moon rises in the east,
the sun sets in the west,
following one another in succession,
separating only to reunite,
ascending is called yang,
descending is called yin.
On earth, it is called principle,
in heaven, it is called pattern.
Condensation is called rain,
dispersion is called wind;
blazing is called fire,
solidification is called ice;
form is called stone,
appearance is called star;
new moon is called dawn,
darkness is called night;
flowing through is called river,
whirling back is called abyss;
level is called soil,
accumulated is called mountain.
Man and woman share the same position,
mountain and marsh communicate their energies,
thunder and wind do not oppose each other,
fire and water do not conflict.
Heaven and earth unite their virtues,
sun and moon follow their light,
nature is one body,
thus all things follow their constant ways,
entering is called hidden,
emerging is called manifest,
the single breath waxes and wanes,
transforming without harm.
Therefore, intense yin and thunder lightning
do not arise differently;
heaven, earth, sun, and moon
are not distinct entities.
Hence it is said:
From the perspective of their differences,
even the liver and gall are as distant as Chǔ and Yuè;
from the perspective of their similarities,
all things are one body.
Humans are born within heaven and earth,
embodying the form of nature.
The body
is the essence of yin and yang.
Nature
is the true character of the five phases;
emotions
are the changing desires of the wandering soul;
spirit
is what heaven and earth use to govern.
Speaking in terms of life,
then nothing lacks longevity;
extending this to death,
then nothing lacks premature end.
Viewed from the small,
nothing is not small;
observed from the large,
nothing is not large.
A child who dies young may be considered long-lived,
while Péng Zǔ may be considered short-lived;
an autumn hair may be large,
while Tài Shān may be small;
thus life and death are a single thread,
right and wrong are one strand.
Distinguishing them,
then beard and eyebrows have different names;
combining them in discourse,
they are but one hair of the body.
The words of the Six Classics
are teachings of division and placement;
the sayings of Zhuāng Zhōu
are expressions of conveying intent.
Approaching it from the grand,
then the ultimate has no exterior;
managing it from the small,
then things have their regulations.
Holding to the numbers of fives and tens,
examining the names of left and right,
is a narrow doctrine;
following nature,
abiding in heaven and earth,
is a discourse of vastness.
All that the ears and eyes prefer,
the application of names and duties,
holding office without changing one's role,
devoting oneself to one's duties,
is not to sever hands and feet,
or dismember limbs.
Yet later generations' lovers of novelty disregard the root,
each speaking only of themselves,
why wait for others?
They harm life and injure nature,
turning into enemies,
cutting and severing limbs,
without feeling pain;
eyes see colors without regard to what the ears hear,
ears listen without awaiting what the heart thinks,
the heart rushes after desires without fitting what nature finds peaceful,
thus when illnesses sprout, life is not fully lived,
and when calamities arise, all things are ruined.
The ultimate person is
serene in life and tranquil in death.
Serene in life, their emotions are not confused;
tranquil in death, their spirit does not depart.
Thus, they can transform with yīn and yáng without changing,
follow the shifts of heaven and earth without shifting themselves.
In life, they fulfill their lifespan;
in death, they follow what is fitting.
Their heart and qì are peacefully regulated,
neither diminishing nor waning.
Hence, Guǎngchéngzǐ dwelled in the Kōngtóng Mountains to enter the gate of infinity,
and Xuānyuán ascended the heights of Kūnlún, leaving behind the root of the mysterious pearl.
This shows that those who submerge themselves easily survive,
while those who stray from the root struggle to endure.
Had Féngyí not encountered Hǎiruò,
he would not have considered himself small;
had Yúnjiàng not lost his Ménghóng,
there would be no way to know his youth.
From this perspective,
those who self-approve do not shine,
those who self-establish do not stand firm.
Guarding what one has provides foundation;
holding to nothing entails no attachment.
The moon wanes then fills;
the sun rises then sets.
The Xiánchí does not linger over Yánggǔ,
and after the chariot is hung, it will soon enter.
Thus, those who seek gains lose,
those who contend for brilliance fail.
The desireless are self-sufficient;
the empty receive substance.
Mountains still and valleys deep—
this is the way of nature;
attaining the way and being upright—
this is the substance of a noble person.
Hence, those who devise cleverness and craft harm things;
those who distinguish right and wrong endanger themselves;
those who adorn themselves to display purity are deluded in life;
those who fear death and revere life lose their integrity.
Thus, if the principles of nature are disrupted,
heaven and earth fall into disorder, and the sun and moon contend to follow,
morning and evening miss their times, and day and night become indistinct;
people compete and chase profit,
straying and galloping recklessly,
fathers and sons discordant,
rulers and ministers alienated.
Therefore, repeating words to seek trust
is the sincerity beneath the bridge;
restraining oneself for others
is the benevolence outside the walls;
stealing and hanging oneself
is the child of a ruined family;
cutting open bellies and slicing flesh
is the minister of a chaotic state;
flaunting essence and adorned with hàngxiè
is the scholar of a benighted age;
treading frost and dew,
covered in dust
is the greedy and reckless commoner;
purifying oneself to blame the world,
cultivating virtue to expose flaws belongs to the slanderers;
elaborating on rights and wrongs,
abandoning substance for ornamentation
is the confused lot;
sincerity not fawning,
seeking trust through appearance—
thus, adorned with pearls and jade to leap into fire and water
is the end of Jié and Zhòu;
eating beans and picking ferns,
starving to death together
is the destitution of Yán Yí.
Hence, when the path of fame and profit opens,
sincerity and faithfulness weaken;
when debates over right and wrong flourish,
pure and honest feelings wither.
Thus, the pinnacle of the ultimate way
is blended into one, undivided,
united as a single body,
where gain and loss go unheard.
Fúxī knotted ropes,
Shénnóng taught farming—
those who opposed it died,
those who complied lived.
How could one know greed and filth as punishment,
and purity and integrity as fame?
Let the essence of ultimate virtue
be nothing beyond this.
Great balance, simple and firm,
unchanging in its order,
clear, quiet, and solitary,
open and empty, waiting—
good and evil undistinguished,
right and wrong uncontested,
so all things return to their place and attain their true nature.
After the Confucians and Mohists,
debates on hardness and whiteness arose together,
fortune and misfortune tied to things,
gain and loss residing in the heart.
They gathered followers and formed cliques,
invading each other with arguments.
Once, the heroes of great Qí,
the scholars of Sān Jìn,
boldly confronted each other,
distinguishing these matters,
all believing a hundred-year life hard to attain,
and the passage of sun and moon unpredictable.
They all enhanced their servants and horses,
adorned their clothing,
beautified pearls and jade,
decorated walls and curtains,
flattered rulers outwardly,
deceived fathers and brothers inwardly,
forced their talents and wisdom,
competed in纵横 strategies,
families ruined by clever sons,
states lost to talented ministers.
Thus, they did not live out their natural years, greatly cutting themselves off amid worldly affairs.
Hence, the trees in the mountains,
with large trunks, remain unharmed.
Countless apertures harmonize together,
suddenly ceasing on their own.
The wild goose's impermanence
lies in lacking substance and muddying its pattern;
death and life unchanged,
yet the turtle is treasured
for knowing fortune and misfortune.
Thus, the ultimate person purifies their substance and muddies their pattern,
unchanged by death and life, and never speaking of it.
Separate words
are talks of embracing the way;
disputations
are the start of virtue's ruin;
divided qì
is a disease of the body;
a divided heart
is a calamity for all things.
Therefore, those who saddle and bridle horses
travel to distant branches;
those who ponder success and failure
sit seeking enemies;
scaling obstacles and attacking dangers
are people of Zhào;
lifting mountains to fill the sea
are people of Yān and Chǔ.
Zhuāng Zhōu, seeing it thus,
expounded the wonders of the way and virtue,
narrated the root of non-action,
used allegories to broaden it,
borrowed things to extend it,
merely to entertain a heart of non-action and wander freely through an age;
how could it be to hope at the gates of Xiányáng or contend in debates at Jìxià?
Those skilled in dealing with people
merely guide them,
without opposition.
Thus, Gōngmèng Jìzǐ appeared in embroidered robes,
yet Mòzǐ did not attack him;
Zhōngshān Zǐmóu's heart was at the palace gate of Wèi,
yet Zhānzǐ did not reject him.
Following their origins,
using their arrivals,
guiding and pacifying them,
letting them settle themselves,
inspiring and opening them,
allowing them to relax themselves.
Moreover, what is Zhuāng Zhōu's writing worth discussing!
Have you not yet heard of the discourse of the Great Beginning,
the subtle words of the profound ancients?
Simply, not harming things, the form is born;
things unharmed, the spirit is clear.
Form and spirit within me, the way and virtue are accomplished;
loyalty and faithfulness unwavering, above and below are balanced.
This allows modern talks to align with antiquity,
uniform in speech but distinct in meaning—
this is the heart able to guard its root,
and the mouth speaking without need for coordination. "
Thereupon, those few individuals,
swayed by the wind and waves,
exchanged tense glances,
retreated in disorder,
stumbling and losing their tracks.
Gazing after them,
their ears later also thus,
knowing they had no substance, dispirited and ashamed in their decline and obscurity.

《樂論》
Liú Zǐ inquired, saying:
"Confucius stated:
'For securing the rulers and governing the people,
nothing is better than rites;
for transforming customs and changing habits,
nothing is better than music.'
Now rites are
that by which men and women are distinguished,
that by which fathers and sons are perfected,
that by which rulers and ministers are established,
and that by which the common people are harmonized;
no instrument of governance takes precedence over this,
therefore for securing rulers and governing people nothing is better than rites.
But metal, stone, silk, bamboo - the sounds of bells, drums, pipes, and strings,
shields, axes, feathers, plumes - the postures of advancing, retreating, bowing, and rising,
what benefit do they bring to governance if present,
what detriment do they cause to transformation if absent,
yet you say 'transforming customs and changing habits nothing is better than music'?"
Master Ruǎn replied:
"Excellent!
Your question.
Formerly Confucius established the general principle,
but had not yet presented its outline.
Now I shall discuss its main points for you,
and you yourself may comprehend the details."
"Now music is
the substance of heaven and earth,
the nature of all things.
Align with its substance,
attain its nature,
then there is harmony;
depart from its substance,
lose its nature,
then there is discord.
When the sages of old created music,
they intended to follow the nature of heaven and earth,
and embody the life of all things,
therefore they established the sounds of heaven, earth, and eight directions,
to correspond with the voices of yin-yang and eight winds,
standardized the pitches of Huángzhōng's balanced harmony,
opened the vital energy of all living things and myriad beings,
thus when pitch pipes harmonize then yin and yang are balanced,
when musical sounds are appropriate then all things are ordered,
men and women do not exchange their places,
rulers and ministers do not violate their positions,
the four seas share the same view,
the nine provinces unify their rhythms,
played at the circular mound, heavenly deities descend,
played at the square peak, earthly spirits respond above;
when heaven and earth unite their virtue then all things unite their life,
punishments and rewards need not be used and the people naturally become tranquil."
"Heaven and earth are simple and easy,
therefore elegant music is not complicated;
the Way and virtue are plain and mild,
therefore without sound and without flavor.
Not complicated then yin and yang naturally connect,
without flavor then all things naturally rejoice,
daily progressing in goodness and completing transformation without self-awareness,
customs change and shift and unite in this music,
this is the Way of spontaneity,
the beginning of music."
"Afterwards, when sages no longer arose,
the Way and virtue became neglected and corrupted,
governance and laws were not established,
knowledge and cunning disturbed things,
transformation was abandoned while desires prevailed,
each had their own customs.
Therefore the teachings created are called 'influences',
what is practiced and followed is called 'customs'.
The influence of Chǔ and Yuè favored bravery,
therefore their custom made light of death;
the influence of Zhèng and Wèi favored licentiousness,
therefore their custom made light of dissipation.
Making light of death,
thus there were songs of rushing into fire and water;
making light of dissipation,
thus there were tunes of Sāngjiān and Púshàng.
Each sang what they favored,
each chanted what they practiced,
those who desired it shed tears,
those who heard it sighed,
turning away and leaving it,
none were not impassioned.
Cherishing day-long pleasures,
embracing night-long sighs,
gathering together to combine them,
forming groups to practice them,
decadently without end,
abandoning the affection between father and son,
relaxing the regulations between ruler and minister,
depleting the rites of household,
neglecting the work of farming,
forgetting the joy of lifelong fulfillment,
exalting customs of licentious indulgence;
therefore south of the Jiāng and Huái the people favored cruelty,
between the Zhāng and Rǔ the people favored elopement,
Wú had the principle of paired swords,
Zhào had the guest who played the zither.
Energy issued from within,
sound entered the ear,
hands and feet flying about,
unaware of their frightfulness."
"Favoring bravery then leads to offending superiors,
licentious abandon then leads to abandoning kin.
Offending superiors then ruler and minister become opposed,
abandoning kin then father and son become discordant;
discord and opposition alternating in conflict,
then troubles arise and disasters start.
Disasters starting then intentions become more divergent,
troubles arising then concerns become different.
Therefore the eight directions had distinct influences,
the nine provinces had different customs,
separated and turned against each other,
unable to communicate,
sounds differing and energies distinct,
melodies and rhythms uneven.
Therefore the sages established harmonizing sounds,
created peaceful tones,
instituted convenient ceremonial rhythms,
determined compliant postures,
so that all under heaven who made music would take them as model.
From above to below,
descending in graded order,
reaching to the common people,
all heard them.
Those singing chants extolled the virtue of former kings,
those bowing and rising practiced the postures of former kings,
those using instruments imitated the patterns of former kings,
those applying measures responded to the systems of former kings;
entering the heart,
sinking into the energy,
heart and energy harmoniously blended,
then customs became uniform."
"When the sages created the postures of advancing, retreating, bowing, and rising,
it was to bend the physical form,
subdue the heart's intent,
facilitate cultivation,
and settle one's duties.
Singing poems and songs,
was to express peace and harmony,
and manifest what is not yet attained.
Bells and drums serve to regulate the ear,
feathers and plumes serve to control the eye,
those listening are not unbalanced,
those watching are not corrupted;
ears and eyes neither unbalanced nor corrupted then customs transform,
therefore for transforming customs and changing habits nothing is better than music.
Thus the eight sounds have their fundamental substance,
the five tones have their spontaneity,
those sharing the same category are ordered by size ruling each other.
Having spontaneity,
therefore they cannot be disordered;
size ruling each other,
therefore they can be balanced.
As for the zither of Kōngsāng,
the lute of Yúnhé,
the pipes of Gūzhú,
the chime stones of Sìbīn,
these objects are all harmoniously pure and even,
their sounds mutually appropriate,
therefore they must have constant positions;
ordered by size ruling each other,
responding to the energy of Huángzhōng,
therefore they must have constant measures.
Having constant positions,
therefore their instruments are precious;
having constant measures,
therefore their construction is not arbitrary.
Being precious,
therefore they can serve the spirits;
not arbitrary,
therefore they can transform people.
These objects connect to the images of heaven and earth,
therefore they cannot be arbitrarily made;
their general resemblance is to the sounds of distant things,
therefore they cannot be arbitrarily changed.
Yǎ and Sòng have distinctions,
therefore humans and spirits are not mixed;
rhythms and combinations have numbers,
therefore variations are not disordered;
circling movements have measures,
therefore bowing and rising are not confused;
singing and chanting have focus,
therefore words are not perverse.
Guiding with goodness,
pacifying with harmony,
maintaining with centeredness,
persisting with endurance;
dispersing their groups,
ordering their patterns,
supporting what dies young,
aiding what lives long,
causing them to abandon biased customs,
and return to the great transformation of sage kings."
"The ancient kings created music
to stabilize the nature of all things,
and unify the minds of the world.
Therefore, they made its sounds tranquil,
and its expressions harmonious.
The subordinates would not covet the ruler's music,
the ruler would not desire the ministers' entertainments,
and without contention between high and low, loyalty and righteousness were accomplished.
Proper music
serves to exclude licentious sounds,
so when music is abandoned, licentious sounds arise.
Emperor Āi of Hàn disliked music,
abolished the Music Bureau,
yet failed to establish proper rituals;
with musical principles neglected,
licentious sounds consequently emerged.
Zhāng Fàng and Chúnyú Chǎng were excessively arrogant and unrestrained,
Bǐng Qiáng and Jǐng Wǔ possessed wealth overflowing in their generation.
After music was abolished,
lower classes became increasingly wanton.
When one personally lacks proper preferences yet debauchery grows worse,
it is because rituals are not established."
"Punishment and education form one body,
rituals and music
are the external and internal aspects.
When punishment is relaxed, education cannot stand alone;
when rituals are abandoned, music has nothing to support.
Defining the distinction between noble and humble,
establishing hierarchy between superior and inferior -
this is called ritual;
people living in peace,
emotions without sorrow -
this is called music.
Carriages, robes, banners, palaces, and food
are the instruments of ritual;
bells, chimes, drums, zithers, and songs
are the tools of music.
When rituals exceed their proper form, nobility and humility become disordered;
when music loses its proper sequence, intimacy and distance become confused.
Rituals establish the forms,
music pacifies the heart;
rituals govern the external,
music transforms the internal;
when rituals and music are correct, the world is at peace."
"When the people of Wèi sought ornate trappings and curved bell-racks, Confucius sighed,
lamenting the deterioration of rituals and collapse of music.
The bell is the master of sounds,
the rack is the system for bells.
When bells lose their proper system, sounds lose their master;
when mastery and system lack constancy, strange sounds emerge together.
The alternation of prosperity and decline follows in succession,
the changes of ancient and modern are as one,
thus when sagely teachings are abandoned, clever people together create extraordinary music.
King Jǐng delighted in the tones of great bells,
King Píng favored the tunes of Shī Yán,
ministers and high officials clapped and marveled,
common people eagerly longed to hear,
proper music was consequently abandoned,
the music of Zhèng greatly flourished,
the odes of Yǎ and Sòng were no longer studied,
while demonic and licentious tunes were sought after.
When Lǐ Yǎnnián created the 'Toppling Cities' song,
Emperor Wǔ longed for seductive beauties;
when Yōngmén composed the 'Pine and Cypress' melody,
King Mǐn thought of garments not yet cold.
Thus when soft and mournful sounds emerge,
and sorrowful, resentful, frivolous lyrics arise,
people later develop intentions of indulgent desires and extravagance,
people later harbor hearts of self-regard and self-indulgence;
therefore the gentleman detests the songs of Dàlíng,
and hates the dances of Běilǐ."
"The ancient kings created music
not to indulge the pleasures of eyes and ears,
nor to glorify the delights of secluded chambers.
It must connect with the energy of heaven and earth,
and calm the spirits of all things;
secure the positions of high and low,
and stabilize the truth of human nature.
Therefore, the songs of the pure temple chant of successful achievements,
the poems of guest feasts praise the principles of ritual deference,
the common people are transformed by their goodness,
different customs submit to their virtue;
this is why licentious sounds are despised,
and proper music is valued."
"Yet rituals change with circumstances,
music transforms with time,
thus the Five Emperors had different systems,
the Three Kings each created differently,
not because they opposed each other,
but to respond to temporal changes.
When common people become accustomed to licentious sounds,
damaging the proper music of ancient kings,
later kings must consequently create new music,
each proclaiming their merit and virtue to the world,
adapting to changes to keep people from weariness.
Yet they only change the names and titles,
alter the compositions and songs,
while the musical sounds themselves
remain peaceful and natural as always;
thus Huángdì chanted of the Cloud Gate spirit,
Shǎohào sang of the phoenix's traces,
the names of 'Xiánchí' and 'Liùyīng' changed,
yet the huángzhōng pitch standard remained unchanged.
Therefore, those who understand the transformations of the Way can examine music,
while those who merely like musical sounds are inadequate to discuss pitch standards."
"Shùn commanded Kuí to oversee music,
teaching the noble youths the virtue of harmony:
'Poetry expresses intent,
song chants the words,
tones follow the chanting,
pitch standards harmonize the tones.
When the eight sounds can be harmonized,
not interfering with their proper order,
spirits and humans are harmonized.'
He also said:
'I wish to hear the six pitch standards, five tones, and eight sounds,
in governing darkness,
to utter and receive the five statements.
You shall listen!'
Complex techniques and licentious sounds
confuse the heart and ears,
causing forgetfulness of peace and harmony,
which the gentleman does not hear.
This means proper music communicates through peace, ease and simplicity,
making the heart clear and energy pure,
enabling one to perceive pitch standards,
and utter and receive the five statements.
Kuí said:
'Strike the sounding stones,
pluck zithers while chanting,
and ancestral spirits will arrive;
with Yú's guests in their places,
all lords deferring in virtue,
below, drums and hand-drums,
together starting and stopping with zhù and yǔ,
sheng and bell alternating,
birds and beasts moving rhythmically;
when the Sháo music of nine movements is completed,
phoenixes come ceremoniously.'
Kuí said:
'When I strike and tap the stones,
all beasts follow dancing,
all officials truly harmonious.'
Poetry expresses intent,
song chants the words,
playing stone chimes and sounding zithers,
with tones following pitch standards,
relating the virtue of ancient kings -
therefore ancestral spirits arrive;
sheng and bell alternating,
proper music sounds sparse,
governance cultivated without harm -
therefore creatures move rhythmically;
music having proper moderation,
nine movements and that is all,
yīn and yáng regulated and flowing,
harmonious energy evenly circulating -
therefore distant birds come ceremoniously;
substantial without ornamentation,
the four seas united -
therefore striking and tapping stones,
all beasts follow dancing.
This means the world is well-governed and peaceful,
all things in their proper places,
sounds not clamorous,
serenely without portents,
therefore all officials are harmonious.
Thus when Confucius in Qí heard the Sháo music,
for three months he didn't notice the taste of meat,
meaning perfect music makes people desireless,
hearts peaceful and energy settled,
not regarding meat as flavorful.
From this perspective,
we know the sage's music is simply harmonious."
"The music from Xīlíng and Qīngyáng was all made from bamboo,
listening to the phoenix's cry,
revering the image of the long wind,
gathering from the great forests,
what was unseen at the time,
what the common people rarely heard,
thus the world embraced its virtue and was transformed by its spirit.
When elegant music circulates universally, all things harmonize;
when it is simple and tranquil, listening is not excessive;
when easy and straightforward, it regulates and commands the spirit;
when calm and dignified, it subdues human hearts:
this was the intention of the ancient kings in creating music.
Since then, the music of decadent times,
its substance is not genuine,
its instruments are not solid,
its system lacks integrity,
drawn from nearby things,
identical to the human world,
each seeking their own preferences,
indulging whatever exists in their minds,
the sounds of the villages compete in loudness,
the music of the long lanes vies to be first,
children gathering to chant of wealth and nobility,
grass-cutters and herdsmen carrying loads singing of poverty and lowliness,
the roles of ruler and minister not yet abandoned,
yet each person harbors ten thousand different hearts."
"At the end of Xiàhòu's reign,
he raised ten thousand women,
clothed them in embroidered silks,
fed them with grain and meat,
their clamoring and morning songs,
those who heard them felt sorrow,
the world suffered from this calamity,
the common people were wounded by its poison.
The last ruler of Yīn,
also played such music,
with pools of wine and forests of meat,
continuing night into day;
yet before the sounds of lament ceased,
enemy states had already seized his zithers and lutes.
A hall full of people drinking,
music played yet tears flow,
this is not because all have sorrow,
but because this music is not joyful.
When the king resided among his ministers,
performing new music in the temple,
all who heard it were moved to sorrowful sobs.
Emperor Huán heard the Chǔ zither,
felt凄怆 and heartbroken,
leaned against the screen and grieved,
sighing deeply with emotion:
'How excellent!
If the zither can be like this,
one is already enough.'
Emperor Shùn ascended Gōnglíng,
passing through Fán streets,
heard birds singing and felt sad,
tears streaming down,
said:
'How beautiful, the birds' song!'
Had his attendants chant it,
saying:
'If stringed sounds were like this,
would it not be joyful!'
This is what is called taking sorrow as joy.
If truly sorrow is considered joy,
then what joy is there in the world?
If the world has no joy,
yet yīn and yáng are harmonized,
disasters do not arise,
that would already be difficult.
Music should
make people's spirits peaceful,
prevent declining energy from entering,
enable heaven and earth to interact smoothly,
distant things come gathering,
therefore it is called joy.
Now it causes flowing tears and agitation,
sobbing that injures the spirit,
cold and heat become unsuitable,
all things do not flourish,
even though produced by strings and bamboo,
it should be called grief—
how can we bow and sigh, calling this joy!
Formerly Jìliúzǐ played the zither facing the wind,
listeners' tears soaked their lapels,
his disciple said:
'How excellently you play the zither!
It is truly sublime.'
Jìliúzǐ replied:
'Joy is called good,
sorrow is called injury;
I play sorrow and injury,
not good joy.'
From this perspective,
strings and bamboo need not produce joy,
singing need not be good,
hence Mòzǐ's condemnation of music.
Alas!
Those who take sorrow as joy—
Hú Pī Xuán drowned in sorrow unchanged,
thus wished to be a commoner;
Lǐ Sī followed sorrow without return,
thus longed to chase the cunning hare;
Alas!
Should not the noble person take warning from this!"
