"Biography of the Great Man"
The Great Man is an elder.
His surname and given name are unknown.
He expounded on the beginning of heaven and earth,
spoke of the matters of Shénnóng and Huángdì,
clearly.
None knew the number of his years lived.
He once dwelt on Sūmén Mountain,
thus the world all called him the recluse.
Nourishing his nature to prolong life,
sharing brilliance with nature itself,
he regarded the affairs of Yáo and Shùn as if in the palm of his hand.
Taking ten thousand lǐ as a single step,
a thousand years as one morning,
traveling without rushing and dwelling without settling,
seeking the great Way yet having no fixed abode.
The gentleman responded to change and followed harmony,
took heaven and earth as his home,
when fortune departed and influence crumbled,
he remained towering and alone,
believing himself sufficient to move with the Creator,
thus silently explored the Way and its virtue,
not sharing the world's ways.
Those who considered themselves good disapproved of him, the ignorant found him strange,
not understanding his subtle spiritual transformations;
yet the gentleman did not change his pursuits due to the world's disapproval and wonder.
The gentleman considered the central region in the world no more significant than a fly or mosquito on a curtain,
thus never regarded it as his concern,
instead directing his will to exotic and strange domains,
traveling, observing, and enjoying,
unseen by the world,
wandering without ultimate destination.
He left his writings on Sūmén Mountain and departed,
the world none knowing where he went.
Someone wrote to the Great Man, saying:
"Under heaven, nothing is more esteemed
than the gentleman:
His attire has prescribed colors,
his countenance follows set norms,
his speech observes fixed measures,
his conduct adheres to constant patterns.
Standing, he bends like a chime stone;
cupping his hands, he embraces an imaginary drum.
His movements and stillness follow rhythm,
his steps move to the shāng and yǔ pitches,
his advances, retreats, and turns
all conform to rules.
His heart is as if holding ice,
trembling with caution,
restraining himself to cultivate conduct,
growing more careful day by day,
choosing where to tread,
fearing any misstep.
He recites the legacy teachings of Zhōu and Confucius,
admires the virtue of Táng and Yú,
cultivates only the law,
restrains himself with ritual.
Holding guī and bì jades,
walking as if following inked lines,
his actions aim to be models for the present,
his words seek to be rules for eternity.
Praised in his youth by the village,
renowned in adulthood throughout the state,
above he aspires to become one of the Three Dukes,
below he won't settle for less than a provincial governor.
Thus he accumulates gold and jade,
dangles embroidered ribbons,
enjoys a revered position,
receives fiefs and lands,
spreads his fame to later ages,
rivals the merits of antiquity;
serving his lord and king,
governing and nurturing the people,
retiring to manage his private estate,
raising his wife and children.
He divines for an auspicious residence,
planning for boundless blessings,
keeping misfortune distant and drawing fortune near,
securing himself firmly forever.
This truly is the lofty aim of scholar-gentlemen,
a beautiful conduct unchanging through past and present.
Now you, sir, dwell with disheveled hair in the vast sea,
far removed from such gentlemen.
I fear the world sighs over you and criticizes you.
Your behavior is laughed at by society,
with no way to advance yourself,
this can indeed be called shameful.
Residing in hardship,
with conduct mocked by the common world,
I do not think you have chosen well, sir."
Thereupon the Great Man sighed deeply,
and responding as if through clouds and rainbows, said:
"How can what you say comprehend anything!
The Great Man
shares substance with the Creator,
exists alongside heaven and earth,
wanders freely in this floating world,
completes himself with the Dào.
Transforming, scattering, gathering,
his form is not constant.
Heaven and earth set boundaries within,
while clarity and openness extend without.
The eternal stability of heaven and earth
is beyond the reach of worldly understanding.
Let me explain to you:
In the past,
heaven was once below,
earth was once above,
turned upside down,
not yet settled firm.
How could one not lose measure and constancy then?
When heaven shifts with earth's movements,
mountains collapse and rivers surge,
clouds scatter and thunder ruins,
when the six directions lose order,
how can you choose where to tread,
or walk to shāng and yǔ pitches?
When vital forces struggled for survival,
all things feared death,
limbs refusing obedience,
bodies turning to mud,
roots uprooted, branches severed,
all losing their place,
how could you restrain yourself and cultivate conduct,
bending like chime stones, embracing drums?
Lǐ Mù achieved merit but died;
Bó Zōng was loyal but his line ended.
Advancing for gain, they lost their lives;
seeking rank and reward, their families perished.
How can you amass billions in gold and jade,
serve your lord fully, and keep wife and children safe?
And have you not seen lice in trousers?
Fleeing into deep seams, hiding in torn padding,
they think they've found auspicious dwellings.
They dare not leave the seam's edge when moving,
nor venture beyond the crotch when active,
believing they follow the inked lines.
Hungry, they bite people,
thinking they have endless food.
But when fierce fires flow,
scorching cities, destroying capitals,
the lice die in the trousers without escape.
How different are you gentlemen in your narrow world from lice in trousers?
Alas!
And you think you keep misfortune distant and draw fortune near,
securing yourselves forever!
Observe the sun-bird roaming beyond the dust,
and the wren playing among reeds and lotus—
great and small simply don't correspond.
Why should I hear about your so-called gentlemen?
Moreover, recently Xià perished by Shāng,
Zhōu shifted to Liú,
Gěng and Bó became ruins,
Fēnghào turned into mounds.
When the perfect man comes for a glance, generations repay;
his dwelling isn't fixed,
others possess it.
With whom will your fiefs and lands last?
Thus the perfect man dwells without settling,
governs without cultivating,
taking the sun and moon as his standard,
yīn and yáng as his schedule.
Why would he cling to worldly sentiments,
bound to a single era?
He comes with eastern clouds,
rides on western winds,
guarding the feminine with yīn,
asserting masculinity with yáng.
His will fulfilled, desires followed,
nothing in the world can exhaust him.
Why would he fail to advance himself and fear the world's laughter?"
"In the past, when heaven and earth opened,
all things were born together.
The great were serene in their nature,
the small tranquil in their form.
Yīn concealed its breath,
yáng emitted its essence.
Harm had nowhere to be avoided,
benefit nothing to contend for.
Released, nothing was lost;
gathered, nothing overflowed.
Death wasn't premature,
life wasn't longevity;
fortune brought no gain,
misfortune no blame.
Each followed its fate,
maintaining its measure.
The bright didn't win by wisdom,
the dim didn't fail by folly;
the weak weren't afraid under pressure,
the strong didn't exhaust their power.
Without lords, all creatures were settled;
without ministers, all affairs were ordered.
Preserving their bodies, cultivating their nature,
they didn't violate their principles.
Only being thus,
could they long endure.
Now you create sounds to confuse hearing,
assume colors to distort form;
externally altering appearance,
internally concealing true feelings,
harboring desires to seek more,
using deceit to pursue fame.
With lords established, tyranny arose;
with ministers appointed, villainy was born.
Sitting, you devise rituals and laws,
binding the common people,
deceiving the foolish, duping the simple,
hiding wisdom, playing god.
The strong glare and bully violently,
the weak haggardly serve others.
Feigning integrity to achieve greed,
inwardly treacherous, outwardly benevolent,
unrepentant when crime arrives,
smug when fortune meets.
Racing along this path to promotion,
thus stuck in stagnation, never rising."
"When there is no nobility, the lowly bear no resentment;
when there is no wealth, the poor do not contend;
each is self-sufficient and without desires.
With no favors to bestow,
there is no one to blame for death or defeat;
without extraordinary sounds, the ear does not crave novelty;
without seductive sights, the eye does not seek diversion;
when ears and eyes remain unchanged, nothing can disturb one's spirit;
this is what the ancient sages ultimately achieved.
Now you honor the worthy to elevate yourselves,
compete in abilities to surpass others,
strive for power to dominate,
and flaunt nobility to overpower;
driving all under heaven to pursue these ends,
this is why superiors and subordinates destroy each other.
Exhausting all things between heaven and earth to satisfy endless desires for sensory pleasures,
this does not nourish the common people.
Then fearing the people would realize this truth,
you offer heavy rewards to please them,
and impose harsh punishments to intimidate them;
when resources deplete and rewards cannot be sustained,
when punishments are exhausted and penalties become unenforceable,
then begin the disasters of fallen states, slain rulers, and collapse.
Is this not the doing of you gentlemen?
Your rituals and laws
are truly methods for mutilating, plundering, throwing into chaos, endangering, and causing death throughout the world;
yet you regard them as beautiful conduct and unchangeable principles,
is this not mistaken!
Now I drift beyond heaven and earth,
befriending the Creator,
breakfasting at Tānggǔ,
drinking at sunset by Xīhǎi,
preparing to transform and shift,
cycling with the Dào from beginning to end,
compared to all things, is this not generous?
Therefore, those unacquainted with spontaneity are unworthy to speak of the Dào,
those blind to clarity cannot comprehend illumination;
this refers to you."
After the gentleman expressed these words,
those in the world fond of novelty found them extraordinary,
the passionate exalted them.
Those who did not understand their substance,
nor see their essence,
guessed at his Dào,
taking the empty reputation,
none recognized its truth,
none comprehended its reality;
though finding it extraordinary and exalting it,
compared to those who previously denounced it as strange,
they were equally insignificant.
The ultimate person,
through unknowing becomes precious,
through unseeing becomes divine;
the way of divine nobility resides within,
while all things operate externally;
thus the world never realizes their function.
In the wilderness of Fúyáo, a recluse saw him and rejoiced,
believing they shared aspirations and paths,
saying:
"Excellent!
Seeing you, I can vent my indignation.
The simple and sincere Dào of high antiquity has been abandoned,
while trivial branches and leftover embellishments flourish together.
Jackals and tigers greedily prey,
myriad creatures innocent,
taking harm as benefit,
losing nature and perishing bodily,
I cannot bear to see it,
so I left to dwell here.
One cannot keep company with humans,
better to neighbor with trees and stones.
Ānqī fled to Péngshān,
Jiǎolǐ submerged in Dānshuǐ,
Bào Jiāo stood until withered,
Láiwéi left and chose death;
it is due to this!
I shall uphold my will and manifest loftiness,
ending here ultimately,
living as birds and dying as beasts,
burying my form and leaving my bones,
never returning to my former life!
Those with aligned aspirations seek each other,
those with shared affinities unite;
I share this with you, sir."
Thereupon the gentleman spread rainbows to screen dust,
tilted a snowy canopy to shade light,
leaned on a jade balustrade pacing,
gathered reins to proceed calmly,
looked back and said to him:
"The Tàichū true person,
root of heaven alone,
concentrates breath and unifies will,
whereby all things exist;
retreating, sees no followers,
advancing, beholds no predecessors;
emanates from northwest establishing order,
opens southeast as a gate;
subtly embodying Dào and lasting joy through Dé,
straddling heaven and earth residing honored.
Thus my body is formed,
hence I dwell without avoiding things;
wherever I gaze is tranquil;
not burdened by things,
wherever I go succeeds;
wandering freely suffices to ease my mind,
floating and rising enough to express my feelings.
Therefore the ultimate person has no abode,
heaven and earth are their lodging;
the ultimate person has no master,
heaven and earth are their domain;
the ultimate person has no affairs,
heaven and earth are their business;
no distinction between right and wrong,
no difference between good and evil;
hence the world receives their beneficence and all things flourish.
As for hating others and loving oneself,
self-approving and criticizing people,
indignantly striving and seeking,
valuing ambition and despising the body,
this indeed is living as birds and dying as beasts—
how can one thereby manifest and gain glory?
Alas!
Your application of mind!
Scorning peace and benefit, forgetting life,
demanding fame, losing the body;
truly no different from them,
why wither away and choose death?
What you admire is not worth mentioning!
I shall leave you now."
Then he raised eyebrows with sweeping gaze,
shook sleeves and adjusted robe,
loosened reins and released whip,
whereupon wind rose and clouds soared.
That person watched him and wept,
grieving over his own aspirations;
clothed in bark of dead trees,
crouching beneath cliffs,
fearing to die before the night's end.
The master passed by the Divine Palace and rested,
rinsed at Wú Spring and journeyed on,
lingering leisurely as he wandered and gazed.
Seeing a woodcutter on the hill,
he sighed and said:
"Will you end your days with this?"
The woodcutter replied:
"Whether this ends my days or not,
what does it matter?
Moreover, the sage holds no attachments,
why such sorrow?
For prosperity and decline transform,
never constant here.
I conceal my talents within,
awaiting the moment in silence.
Sūn Bìn, with feet cut, captured Péng Juān;
Fàn Jū, ribs broken, then found rest;
Bǎilǐ Xī, in hardship, aided Qín's rise;
Jiāng Zǐyá, in old age, supported Zhōu.
Reversals come anew,
thus first hardship, then harvest follows.
Qín crushed six states,
annexing their lands,
wiping out the feudal lords,
facing south as emperor,
adorned in splendor,
exalting extravagance,
quarried the Southern Mountains for gates,
marked the Eastern Sea as his portal,
gateways to countless homes unbroken,
planning endless eternity,
beautifying palaces with lavish drapes,
striking bells and drums to proclaim his glory,
expanding parks and deepening pools,
rising north of the Wèi to build Xiányáng.
Trees had yet to form forests,
but thorns already crowded Ēpáng.
Ages exist and alternate,
so first gain, then loss ensues;
the exiled captives from east of the mountains rose to rule the world.
Viewing from this,
how can one know hardship or success?
Moreover, the sage takes virtue as heart,
not wealth or rank as aim,
using non-action as utility,
not busying with human affairs,
honor adds no weight,
poverty brings no self-disparagement,
loss not seen as shame,
gain not seen as glory.
A tree's roots firm, branches spread far,
leaves flourish, blossoms fall;
endless death is like a single day's life,
how much of the self
is worth striving for!"
Then, sighing, he sang:
"The sun sets west of Bùzhōu,
the moon rises from Dān Yuān,
the sun's light hidden unseen,
the moon's glow reigns in its stead,
briefly it stands serene,
fading, it moves east again.
Parting and joining like clouds and mist,
coming and going as the swirling wind.
Wealth and honor in a moment's glance,
poverty and lowliness need not last.
Liú Hóu rose from a fugitive,
his might resounding through barbaric lands;
Shào Píng, enfeoffed at Dōnglíng,
in one dawn became a commoner.
Branches and leaves rely on roots,
life and death share rise and fall;
success follows fate's ascent,
decline falls with the times.
Cold and heat march in turn,
change pushes each other on;
fortune and misfortune have no fixed master,
why worry about no return?
Reasoning thus from this truth,
why grieve over bearing firewood!"
Hearing this, the master
smiled and said:
"Though not reaching the great,
you've avoided the petty."
Then he sang:
"Heaven and earth unravel, the cosmos opens,
stars fall, sun and moon crumble,
I soar upward—what shall I cherish!
Robes unadorned yet beautiful,
garb unembellished yet radiant,
wandering above and below—who knows my constancy?
So I left, drifting afar,
unleashing cloud-carriages,
raising aura-canopies,
meandering and circling beyond the vast expanse.
Raising long stars as banners,
striking thunder's rumble,
opening Bùzhōu to drive forth chariots,
treading the nine wilds in peace.
Sitting in the central land, I glance around,
gaze at lofty mountains and turn away,
steady my pace, flying pennants,
letting my mind roam the remote borders.
Choosing not to cultivate former paths,
galloping through obscurity, far and free,
abandoning the multitude's worldly tasks,
what trivial matters are worth reliance?
Ethereal in form, I rise lightly,
subtle in essence, rich in spirit.
Commanding Yí Yì to restrain the sun,
summoning Xīn Lái to gentle the wind.
Climbing Fúsāng's long branches,
ascending Fúyáo's lofty peak.
Leaping into the gloom of hidden winds,
cleansing in the brightness of radiant light.
Leaving garments unworn,
clad in cloud vapor, I journey on.
At dawn, I ride to Yánggǔ,
by dusk, rest steeds at Cháng Quán,
as Yānzī shifts the air,
gleaming like blossoms illuminating darkness.
Left, the crimson sun raising standards,
right, the dark moon planting flags,
changing appearance and altering measures,
I soar stealthily on a long march.
Yīn and Yáng alternate in stride,
the four seasons rush in succession.
Only immortality's transformation is swift,
my heart finds no joy in long stays.
Startling winds surge, leaving music behind,
though clouds rise, I forget sorrow.
Suddenly, lightning vanishes, spirit freed,
traversing the void, roaming afar.
Adorned with sun and moon, radiating light,
I ascend, drifting upward afloat.
Halting advance on that distant path,
I'll set foot in the empty realm.
Sweeping the Purple Palace, laying mats,
sitting in the celestial hall, suddenly feasting,
gathering all sounds in music's play,
tones ethereal and endless,
the Five Emperors dance in succession,
the Six Spirits sing in alternating cycles.
Music chirping, solemn and pure,
piercing the heart, reaching the spirit,
transcending the boundless vast,
the heart ventures, forgetting return,
thoughts grand, ambition proud.
Ceasing the great man's subtlety, not turning back,
I lift cloud-breath upward,
summoning the Jade Maiden of the Great Abyss,
welcoming the Fair One of the High King,
bodies fluid as cloud vapor,
clad in the purity of the supreme clarity,
sharing joy in subtle bestowal,
first, beauty overflowing like divinity,
splendid forms radiant together,
colors brilliant and vibrant,
dark tresses cascading to the temples,
glowing rosy cheeks renewed.
Time dims, soon to fade,
winds flutter, shaking garments.
Clouds part, mist disperses,
haze scatters, forever gone.
Heart bewildered, thoughts wander far,
gazing distantly, no dawn in sight.
Raising clear winds as banners,
wings whirling, I return to expansion.
Soaring through fiery light, leaving borders,
commanding Zhùróng to dispatch.
Driving Xuánmíng to grasp firmness,
Rùshōu wielding halberds ahead,
Gōumáng holding the chariot pole,
floating swiftly on morning clouds.
Vast and boundless, without capital,
alone, unmatched in solitude.
Leaning on the jade balustrade, I glance once,
grieving for the weary world below.
Dividing right and wrong as conduct,
how can it compare to such?
Rainbow banners flutter, cloud flags misty,
joyful wandering—beyond the heavens."
The Great Man, with hair flowing and sideburns flying,
wears robes of patterned splendor,
girded by the belt of Fúyáng.
He holds rare fungi in his mouth,
chews sweet blossoms,
inhales the floating mists,
feasts on dawn's rosy clouds,
rises with the morning clouds,
soars on the spring breeze,
stirring east of the Supreme Ultimate,
wandering west of Kūnlún.
Dropping reins and casting aside whips,
he gazes upon the capitals of Yáo and Shùn,
lost in thought,
melancholy as if forgetting all,
sighing with deep emotion,
saying:
"Alas!
The moment is not like the year,
the year not like heaven,
heaven not like the Dào,
the Dào not like the divine.
The divine is
the root of spontaneity.
Those bustling about deem themselves noble in this world;
how could they know the world holds this in contempt!
Thus, contending with the world for nobility,
nobility is not worthy of honor;
contending with the world for wealth,
wealth is not worthy of precedence.
One must transcend the world and sever ties with the crowd,
leave customs behind and wander alone,
ascending before the Great Beginning,
viewing the dawn of vast emptiness,
thoughts flowing through the boundless,
will expansive and freely stretching,
drifting through the four seasons,
soaring and hovering in the eight directions.
Wishing to follow indulgence and be as if in a trance,
vast and unconstrained—petty conduct is not enough to bring disgrace,
sages and worthies are not enough to bring praise,
transforming and shifting,
supported by the divine intelligence.
Expanding the boundless to dwell therein,
encircling the cosmos as one's abode,
strengthening the eight dimensions to reside in peace,
relying on the control of things to dwell eternally:
In this way, one may be called wealthy and noble.
Therefore, not aligning virtue with Yáo and Shùn,
not sharing merits with Tāng and Wǔ;
Wáng and Xǔ are not fit to be peers,
how could Yángqiū compare in stature?
Heaven and earth cannot surpass his longevity,
what has Guǎngchéngzǐ to stand alongside him?
Stirring the eight winds to raise his voice,
treading the lofty path of supreme auspiciousness;
clad in the nine heavens, opening and clearing,
riding clouds to驾驭飞龙,
mastering above and below to govern all,
distinguishing past and present without conformity;
how could the world's fame and profit burden him!
Thus, lifting Qí and treading on Chǔ,
grasping Zhào and stepping on Qín,
in less than a morning, the world has no rivals,
east, west, south, north, none can stand as neighbors.
Alas!
Your adornments and refinements,
in my view,
where will they endure?"
Thereupon, the master departed into the vast expanse,
through boundless and trackless depths,
flowing and spreading overflowingly,
crossing deep abysses,
leaping over the blue sky,
looking back and gazing afar.
Then, there was carefree wandering for eternal years,
no existence, suddenly merging,
scattering and descending not to arrive,
swiftly parting and dispersing,
billowing and overflowing,
whirlwinds surging, clouds floating,
reaching to Yáoguāng,
racing straight into the midst of the Great Beginning,
and resting in the palace of non-action.
What is the Great Beginning like?
No after, no before,
none can fathom its limits,
who knows its root?
Vast, faint, and continuous,
it returns to where the great Dào exists,
none can fully explore it,
who understands its root?
Opening the nine spirits to seek,
what is enough to elevate oneself?
Ascending its myriad heavens to see comprehensively,
bathing in the harmonious breeze of the great beginning.
Floating carefree to wander far,
following the endless great path.
Leaving Tàiyǐ unattended,
soaring over heaven and earth, walking directly.
Transcending Hóngméng and leaving distant traces,
left, sweeping through wilderness without bounds,
right, dark and remote without direction,
above, listening afar without sound,
below, gazing long without pattern,
applying non-being to house the spirit,
eternally in the great purity, soaring freely.
Lofty mountains towering, dark clouds surging,
northern winds sweeping fiercely, white clouds scattering,
accumulated ice like ridges, cold injuring people.
Yīn and Yáng displaced, sun and moon falling,
earth splitting, rocks cracking, forests and trees destroyed,
great cold, Yáng congealed, chill wounding the heart.
Yáng harmony faint, strong Yīn exhausted,
seas frozen still, cotton wadding snapping,
breath blocked, cold causing splits.
Qì merging, alternating movements divine-like,
cold leading, heat following, harm injuring people,
harmonious with the true man, embracing the great purity.
Spirit focused, intent serene,
cold and heat not harming, none alarmed,
no cause for worry, primal qì calm.
Floating mists reaching the sky, freely passing through,
coming and going subtly, path unshaken,
delighting in what is not of the world, what to contend for?
All others will die, I alone live.
The true man wanders,
driving eight dragons,
shining like sun and moon,
bearing cloud banners,
lingering leisurely,
joyful wherever he goes.
The true man wanders,
the great steps leveled,
the plains opened,
heaven's gate wide,
drizzle misty,
wind rustling,
ascending Huángshān,
emerging from rest,
rivers clear,
Luò free of dust.
Clouds dissipate,
the true man comes.
The true man comes,
only joy abounds!
Times change,
delights decay,
the true man leaves,
returning with heaven.
Back to the endless,
prolonging years of life,
alone, aloof from the world,
gazing at me,
when will he return?
The path stretches endlessly,
the road grows farther daily.
The master has departed from here,
none in the world know his ultimate end,
soaring over heaven and earth, roaming with floating brightness without beginning or end,
the utmost truth of spontaneity.
The magpie does not cross the Jì River,
the Luò does not pass the Wèn,
ordinary people of the world
are also thus.
They have not even traversed regions,
how much less beyond the four seas,
outside heaven and earth?
As for the master,
he regards heaven and earth as an egg.
For petty beings and insignificant folk to discuss his length and shortness,
debate his right and wrong,
is it not lamentable!

Ruǎn Jí's Ten Poems in Four-Character Lines
"Ruǎn Jí's Ten Poems in Four-Character Lines"
The sun blazes fiercely,
while plants and trees stand desolate.
Valley winds fan the summer heat,
dense clouds bring heavy shade.
Lightning flashes and rumbles,
swift thunder leaves its echoes.
Drizzling rain gathers and falls,
drifting and soaking the northern woods.
A light boat floats along,
now rising, now sinking.
Moved by the past, mourning what is to come,
cherishing antiquity, grieving the present.
Life is bound by fate,
as time passes, worries deepen.
How to express these thoughts?
By whistling, singing, and chanting aloud.
Who can uphold their will,
like jade or gold?
In sorrow, not overwhelmed,
in joy, not indulgent.
Humbly receiving the wise teachings,
to comfort my heart.
Celestial images shine in rotation,
as yīn and yáng follow their paths.
The autumn wind blows fiercely early on,
white dew falls by night.
Tall trees wither and fall,
lush grasses lose their glory.
The good times swiftly pass,
the morning sun tilts westward.
All things have a beginning and an end,
who can remain full forever?
The Tài Wēi constellation opens the way,
with three luminaries shedding their light.
Majestic are the flock of dragons,
leaping and soaring in the purple court.
Scales scattered, they decline in weariness,
sometimes soaring high, the path clear.
Now hidden, now silent,
concealing their forms and shadows.
I wish to preserve this day,
forever matching a long life.
The celestial sphere turns swiftly,
as the four seasons alternate in succession.
Winter days are bleak and desolate,
dark clouds veil the sky.
Pure ice covers the marshes,
white snow clings to the mountains.
□□ passes away,
like those flowing rivers.
Who among men does not die?
The noble aim is to preserve one's name intact.
The great way is level and broad,
yet small paths compete to lead.
The dark and yellow are dust and grime,
while red and purple gleam brightly.
Alas, my Confucius,
sage-like and profound, penetrating the mysteries.
Glory not rooted in righteousness,
vanishes like dust and smoke.
Though lacking divine virtue,
I wish to hide in the depths.
Morning clouds gather from all directions,
spreading out by day and night.
Pure light casts its rays,
the bright stars shimmer brilliantly.
Solemnly soar the phoenixes,
harmoniously cry the wild geese.
If I do not rejoice now,
the years will grow late.
Old man Jiāng aided the Zhōu,
Zǐfáng supported the Hàn.
They responded to their time, aiding destiny,
achieving merits and quelling chaos.
Their persons were employed, their deeds illustrious,
their virtues praised through their names.
In this age, there are no past affairs,
and tools are not for current use.
Entrusting fate has its □,
accepting heaven's will without complaint.
Alas, you gentlemen,
why sigh forever?
The sun and moon shine gloriously,
able to mirror heaven's wisdom.
Three sovereigns presided over the court,
and the three and eight rose to prominence.
They elevated the talented and outstanding,
and dismissed the stubborn and wicked.
The highest virtue is to establish moral integrity,
the next is to achieve meritorious deeds.
The wind of benevolence spreads widely,
mysterious transformations silently penetrate.
Fortunate to encounter this prosperous era,
I witness this harmonious time.
Dwelling idly by a humble gate,
I follow only my aspirations.
Advancement and reclusion are different paths,
looking up and down, appearances differ.
Gazing and sighing at ancient heroes,
my thoughts strive to match their lofty traces.
I praise this Jīshān,
and overlook that Yú Dragon.
Ascending high to gaze afar,
I survey all eight directions.
Mountains and rivers stretch endlessly,
long roads diverge and vary.
Moved by that Mòzǐ,
I cherish this Yáng Zhū.
Holding my shadow, standing like a crane,
lifting my head, pacing hesitantly.
Looking up at the soaring birds,
glancing down at the swimming fish.
Red forests veiled in clouds,
green leaves stirred by the breeze.
Creation is vast and mysterious,
all things flourish in abundance.
Excess leads to insufficiency,
moderation brings surplus.
How to nurture one's will?
By guarding it with emptiness and humility.
Still, I wish in another life,
to share the same symbol for ten thousand years.
Humble are we, my kind,
orderly are the great plans.
Delving deeply into classical texts,
our thoughts linger in contemplation.
Then I command my servant,
to set out on a journey.
Vast is the great river,
floating is the poplar-wood boat.
Gazing up at the shining light,
looking down at the flowing waves.
The sun and moon move eastward,
the shining light fades in the west.
Cold departs, heat arrives,
the four seasons alternate in cycle.
Luxuriant blooms flourish in spring,
dense leaves fall in autumn.
Prime years decline with age,
suddenly fleeting as a float,
carefree and at ease,
without blame in this world.
I journey to the northern woods,
wandering by that riverbank.
Reaching up to grasp jade branches,
looking down at plain silk lines.
The hidden phoenix rests its wings,
the lurking dragon leaps its scales.
Dim light conceals their shadows,
their forms transform in response to the divine.
The gentleman advances in virtue,
living frugally, thinking purely.
Amassing wealth invites criticism,
while a simple life earns praise for benevolence.
Yíshū gathered ferns,
their purity and nobility resonated afar.
Lord Jǐng of Qí had a thousand steeds,
yet they turned to dust like this.
Alas, you later generations,
excel in these human relations.
A wicker gate and a small opening,
are deemed the true way.
Huáróng's dazzling beauty,
Unparalleled through the ages.
Enchantingly exquisite,
Graceful like clear ripples.
Dark hair and delicate brows,
Eternal flowing radiance.
Ornate splendor and lavish elegance,
Scent carried by the wind.
Turning back in spiritual awakening,
Soul soaring high.
The nobleman restrains himself,
Heart pure as ice and frost.
In chaotic dimness,
Were the two kings of old.
Jade towers and gem chambers,
Long nights on golden beams.
The Yīn overthrew Xià,
Zhōu cut down Zhòu of Shāng.
Alas, later generations,
May grieve for this.
Morning wind sweeps the dust,
Dawn rain sprinkles the road.
Galloping steeds like dragons leaping,
Neighing mournfully, gazing outward.
Grasping reins and checking whips,
Advancing and retreating with measure.
Joy departs, sorrow comes,
Disconsolate, the heart awakens.
Thinking of that respectful man,
Longingly turning to look back.
Sun and moon move on,
The year draws to its close.
Alas, I, a young man,
Stubborn and unyielding.
Is it not ambition far-reaching,
Yet talent falls short of emulation.
Fate is not like metal or stone,
The body lighter than morning dew.
How can one know Sōng and Qiáo,
Nourishing spirit in primal purity?
Roaming beyond the mundane realm,
Attaining my allotted years.
Poem
Heaven and earth misty and vast,
Primordial essence cycles in order.
Clear brightness shines with splendor,
Harmonious energy at ease.
In the glorious imperial court,
Yī Héng serves as minister.
My talent unfit for civil arts,
My ability unsuited for martial ways,
I go to Yuán and Xiāng rivers,
Seeking refuge with an old fisherman.
Leisurely!
Carefree!
There I dwell, there I stay.
The moon bright, stars sparse,
Sky high, air cold.
Chanting songs, heart wounded,
Awake or asleep, speaking alone.
Facing wine, stroking my chest,
Before food, forgetting to eat.
The world lacks xuāncǎo grass,
Making me sigh in sorrow!
